title: Sebastian and the Extraction
premise: Ines Crane, a burned-out private security contractor, is approached by a stranger claiming she once saved his life—a favor she has no memory of—and he calls in the debt: extract Dr. Elias Voss, a defector carrying evidence that will detonate at an upcoming intelligence summit. As Ines moves Voss across Europe, she realizes he may be deliberate bait in a trap set by her own former agency to flush out leaks like her, and that the stranger's 'favor' is a fabrication designed to bind her to the operation. Torn between loyalty to the few people who trust her and the truth about what really happened on the night she can't remember, Ines chooses truth over survival, exposing the trap at the summit itself. She loses her anonymity and nearly her life, but walks away with Voss alive, the evidence public, and—for the first time since the incident—able to sleep.
about_author: Beatrix Winterbourne is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction. She lives off-grid somewhere along the Baltic coast and refuses all interviews.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Working a dull corporate protection detail in Riga, Ines is cornered by a soft-spoken stranger named Marek who claims she pulled him from a burning car in Prague—something she cannot recall. He leaves a burner phone and a warning: the debt comes due soon. Beat: unease planted beneath routine.

chapters.title: Nights Without Sleep
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Flashbacks fragment through her insomnia—the incident three years ago that ended her agency career, a colleague dead, her memory of the night full of holes. Marek calls: the favor is extraction work, one client, forty-eight hours. Beat: dread sharpening into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Client
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She meets Dr. Elias Voss in a Tallinn safehouse: a defector carrying encrypted files tied to the upcoming Vienna summit. He's charming, frightened, and insists someone inside her old agency sold him out. Ines takes the job for the money she tells herself. Beat: commitment made under false pretenses.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. First leg of the route—ferry to Helsinki under forged papers. Voss probes her past; she deflects. A tail appears that shouldn't know the route. Beat: first crack in the plan, first flicker of trust between them.

chapters.title: Marek's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Revealed: Marek works for a broker called the Cartographer, and the 'saved life' story was scripted to recruit Ines specifically. His growing guilt over deceiving her complicates his orders. Beat: dramatic irony established—reader knows what Ines doesn't.

chapters.title: Helsinki Station
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ambush at the rail terminal; Ines kills a man wearing gear identical to her old agency's kit. Voss sees her competence and something colder underneath. They reroute to Stockholm. Beat: adrenaline high curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Files Say
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss decrypts part of his cargo and learns the summit evidence implicates Operation Nightjar—the same op from Ines's incident. He begins wondering whether he was sent as bait to draw out whoever kept Nightjar's secrets. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The Cartographer reveals the true objective: not protecting Voss but using him to identify the leak—Ines herself, the only survivor who walked away with Nightjar's memory intact. Marek objects; he's reminded of his own debts. Beat: stakes inverted, trap defined.

chapters.title: Stockholm Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Laid low while contacts forge new documents, Ines and Voss circle each other's truths. She admits fragments of the incident; he doesn't tell her what the files say about her. An almost-kiss interrupted by a surveillance sweep. Beat: intimacy against duty.

chapters.title: Old Friends
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines reaches out to Dana, her former partner and only friend, for route help—breaking her own rule about trust. Dana agrees too quickly. Beat: warmth shadowed by the reader's suspicion.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts Ines: what if you're not my guard but my handler? What if I'm the lure? Ines denies it and almost believes herself—but the tail patterns fit an agency playbook only she would recognize. Beat: paranoia becomes mutual.

chapters.title: Crossing the Sound
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Night crossing to Copenhagen goes wrong; Dana's tip-off proves stale or poisoned. Ines must choose between the planned route and a suicidal detour Voss proposes. She chooses Voss. Beat: loyalty shifting from institution to person.

chapters.title: Marek Breaks Pattern
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Ordered to confirm Ines's location for the strike team, Marek instead sends a partial warning—an anonymous text. The Cartographer notices the delay. Beat: the deceiver turns double agent out of conscience.

chapters.title: Copenhagen, Cold Open
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marek finally meets Ines face-to-face and confesses the fabricated favor, the recruitment, the trap. Ines's world tilts: the incident, the insomnia, the job—all engineered to herd her here. Beat: devastating revelation, rage and clarity.

chapters.title: The Memory Returns
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With Marek's dossier as trigger, Ines reconstructs the buried night: she didn't fail on Nightjar—she refused an order to let Voss's predecessor die, and the agency erased her memory of it. Her insomnia was her mind refusing the lie. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Three Ways Out
chapters.summary: Ines, Voss, and Marek argue options: run, sell the files, or go to Vienna and detonate the truth publicly at the summit. Running means living hunted forever. Ines votes for Vienna. Beat: decision point—truth chosen over survival.

chapters.title: The Strike Team
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The Cartographer dispatches the team, including Dana, who has been compromised since chapter ten. Marek feeds the Cartographer a false approach route, buying hours he may not be able to repay. Beat: clock tightening, betrayal layered on betrayal.

chapters.title: Vienna Before the Summit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Infiltration of the summit venue via a maintenance contract Ines once audited. Voss prepares to testify; Marek holds the door; Dana finds them. Beat: calm before the storm, every debt converging.

chapters.title: The Extraction Reversed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Climax. Dana's team breaches; in the firefight Ines refuses to shoot Dana, talking her down instead—refusing the agency's arithmetic of acceptable losses. Voss reaches the press gallery. Marek takes a bullet meant for Ines. Beat: love and loyalty weaponized against duty.

chapters.title: Nightjar, Public Record
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. Voss's files go live mid-summit; delegates scatter; the Cartographer's network burns its own channels to escape exposure. Dana stands down and disappears into the crowd. Beat: catharsis through exposure rather than violence.

chapters.title: Debts Settled
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Aftermath: Marek survives, barely; the 'favor' is finally real—he gave her the truth when lying would have been easier. Ines declines both the agency's quiet reinstatement and Voss's invitation to disappear together. Beat: bittersweet accounting of costs.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Epilogue. Months later, in a rented room far from any client list, Ines reads news of resignations cascading from the summit leak. She sets no alarm, checks no exits, and sleeps through the night. Beat: resolution—the price paid, and peace purchased.
